ci.lane: backend (manage.py test covers broker_catalogue + approvals + the ADR-governance test)

commands: cd backend && .venv/bin/python manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run broker_catalogue  (no changes in broker_catalogue)
cd backend && .venv/bin/python manage.py test broker_catalogue approvals --parallel 1
cd backend && .venv/bin/python manage.py report_catalogue_readiness --broker ... (READ-ONLY; proven in tests against a migrated DB)
cd backend && .venv/bin/python manage.py register_capture_candidate --broker-id dominion_markets ... (DRY-RUN; writes nothing without --commit + flag)
expected_results: A DB-level BEFORE UPDATE trigger prevents mutating a CatalogueArtefact whose version is not DRAFT via ORM save, raw QuerySet.update() and bulk_update, mirroring the ORM save-guard and closing the raw-UPDATE bypass.

A read-only readiness evaluator reports stable per-broker eligibility + reason codes (ELIGIBLE / ALREADY_ACTIVE / SANITISER_NOT_PASS / NO_APPROVED_ARTEFACT / NEEDS_CAPTURE / NOT_CAPTURED / DUPLICATE_SERVER_CONFLICT) without mutating anything.

A governed NEEDS_CAPTURE candidate workflow records a Dominion-style placeholder (identity + non-PII server hint only), DARK/default-OFF, and NEVER creates an artefact/approval/SHA/version; STOP at NEEDS_CAPTURE.
006C v1, v0.2 and the existing Broker Catalogue V1 mechanism behaviour are unchanged; the ADR-governance uniqueness test passes with 0078; secret scan clean; no PII in the diff.
actual_results: broker_catalogue + approvals suite: Ran 111 tests OK (86 pre-existing + 25 new Stream A). makemigrations --check: no changes detected in broker_catalogue (the unrelated strategies index-rename diffs are a pre-existing local Django-version naming artefact, not from this change).

Immutability (tests_immutability_trigger, 6 tests): DRAFT artefact mutable via ORM + raw update; once ACTIVE/RETIRED the ORM save raises ValidationError and the raw update()/bulk_update()/version-repoint raise a DB error (trigger), bytes-pin intact. Trigger is PostgreSQL-only (ORM guard covers other backends); the raw-SQL assertions skip on non-PostgreSQL.

Readiness evaluator (tests_readiness_evaluator, 11 tests): every reason code exercised; a PENDING approval is never ELIGIBLE; duplicate server names flip both brokers to DUPLICATE_SERVER_CONFLICT; evaluation creates/deletes nothing (read-only proven by before==after counts).

Capture candidate (tests_capture_candidate, 8 tests): dry-run default and commit-without-flag write nothing; commit+flag creates NEEDS_CAPTURE only; re-register refreshes descriptive fields but never regresses a CAPTURED status; the workflow NEVER creates an artefact/approval/version (asserted). Command dry-run and read-only report verified.

ADR governance: core.tests_adr_governance 3 tests OK — ADR-0078 introduces no cross-directory duplicate. secret scan: no findings; test_no_secrets OK. One existing test renamed detect->prevent (see limitations).

Command smoke against the DEV DB was not exercised because the dev DB is not migrated for broker_catalogue and the no-DB-mutation hard stop forbids migrating it; the commands are proven against a migrated test DB by the unit tests.
limitations: Repository-only / synthetic-only / DARK: no artefact capture/creation/approval, no catalogue build/activation/staging, no terminal staging/preseed/restart/login, no host/NAS/Wayond contact, no real Gmail/MT5/broker/credentials/PII, no deployment, no public publication. The PR is auto-merge OFF and is NOT merged without a new Sponsor authorisation.

One EXISTING test changed (called out): broker_catalogue/tests.py test_byte_mutation_after_activation_detected -> test_byte_mutation_after_activation_prevented. Its former mechanism (a raw update() simulating a post-activation DB tamper) is now refused by the DB trigger (a strictly stronger guarantee); the test now asserts prevention. Out-of-band host-byte drift detection remains covered by test_manifest_field_tamper_detected and preseed-time re-hashing.
The DB immutability trigger is PostgreSQL-only; on other backends the ORM save-guard is the sole enforcement (the migration is a vendor-guarded no-op there). CI + prod are PostgreSQL.

Artefact-approval state is prod-DB/VPS/Notion (not committed to the repo), so on a fresh DB the readiness evaluator honestly reports NOT_CAPTURED / NO_APPROVED_ARTEFACT for the four brokers; it does not and cannot assert prod approval state.

Dominion Markets remains NEEDS_CAPTURE: no authoritative servers.dat/server id is captured; only the governed candidate workflow is scaffolded here. Artefact capture/approval for Dominion (and the DARK v3 carry-forward that would activate the approved TradersWay/Vantage artefacts) are separate, Sponsor/host-gated steps, NOT in this packet.
Streams B (withdrawal adapters), C (public privacy) and D (MT5 telemetry + Wayond export) are separate PRs and are NOT begun; per the Sponsor they await review of this Stream A response.
